note: Source says the two officers fill their places (the new generals') until their arrival; candidate says 'his place' and 'the colleagues arrived', confusing the referents.
replacement: Such were the contents of Nicias’s letter. When the Athenians had heard it, they refused to accept his resignation. Instead they chose him two colleagues, naming Menander and Euthydemus, two of the officers at the seat of war, to fill their places until the others arrived, so that Nicias would not be left alone in his sickness to bear the whole weight of affairs. They also voted to send out another army and navy, drawn partly from the Athenians on the muster-roll and partly from the allies. The colleagues chosen for Nicias were Demosthenes, son of Alcisthenes, and Eurymedon, son of Thucles. Eurymedon was sent off at once, about the time of the winter solstice, with ten ships and a hundred and twenty talents of silver, and with instructions to tell the army that reinforcements would arrive and that care would be taken of them. Demosthenes stayed behind to organize the expedition. He meant to start as soon as it was spring, sent to the allies for troops, and meanwhile got together money, ships and heavy infantry at home.
